simple.meaning: טָבַח (ṭâbach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to slaughter (animals or men).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, Psalms, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 43:16. Its contexts include death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָבַח (H2873).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: טָבַח (ṭâbach) / H2873 is traced through Genesis 43:16, Exodus 21:37, Deuteronomy 28:31, 1 Samuel 25:11 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”

Your ox will be slain before your eyes, and you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be violently taken away from before your face, and will not be restored to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and you will have no one to save you.
Shall I then take my bread, my water, and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men who I don’t know where they come from?”
The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow,
But I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter. I didn’t know that they had devised plans against me, saying,
“I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter,
“The youth and the old man lie on the ground in the streets.
I have set the threatening sword against all their gates,

definitions.full: H2873. tabach [ טָבַח ] verb slaughter, butcher, slay (Late Hebrew id. (rare) and derivatives; Phoenician טבח participle; Assyrian ‰abâ—u Asrb Annals iii. 56 ; Aramaic , טְבַח (rare) and derivatives; Arabic cook meat, also bake bread; Ethiopic slay ) — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular suffix וּטְבָחוֺ consecutive Exodus 21:37; 3 feminine singular טָֽבְחָה Prov 9:2 ; 2 masculine singular טָבַחְתָּ Lam 2:21 ; 1 singular טָבַחְתִּי 1Sam 25:11 ; Imperative וּטְבֹחַ Gen 43:16 ; Infinitive construct טְבֹחַ Ezek 21:15 ; לִטְבֿוֺחַ Psa 37:14 3 t. (so Baer; van d. H לִטְבּוֺחַ , except לִטְב֑וֺחַ Jer 51:40 ); Passive participle טָבוּחַ Deut 28:31 ; — 1 slaughter, butcher animals for food Exodus 21:37 (E), Prov 9:2 (figurative of Wisdom's furnishing her table); so with accusative of congnate meaning with verb ׳ט טֶבַח Gen 43:16 (J), ׳ט טִבְחָה 1Sam 25:11 ; compare also Deut 28:31 , where punishment lies in fact that the owner does not eat of the slain ox; לִטְבֿ֑וֺחַ יוּבַל אַלּוּף כְּכֶשֶׂב Jer 11:19 like a mild lamb that is led to slaughter , simile of the prophet exposed to his enemies, 51:40 simile of ׳י s vengeance upon Babylon (see also טִבְחָה טֶבַח, ), 25:34 of kings and rulers, under figure of shepherds & choice sheep. 2 in poetry & figurative, slay, kill ruthlessly , with accusative of person Psa 37:14 ; absolute Lam 2:21 (|| הָרַג ; opposed to חמל ); with accusative of congnate meaning with verb ׳ט טֶבַח Ezek 21:15 of a sword sharpened for the slaughter of Israel in judgment.
